lessons.title: Meet artificial intelligence
lessons.subtitle: Understand what an AI assistant can and cannot do
lessons.body:
Artificial intelligence is software that performs tasks such as recognising patterns, making predictions, or generating content. Generative AI produces new text, images, or other output from patterns learned during training. Training adjusts a model using examples; using a trained model to answer a prompt is called inference. Asking an assistant a question is not the same as training your own model.

An assistant can help you draft a study plan, but its answer can contain mistakes. You remain responsible for checking and choosing what to use. Offline lesson packs work without internet; an online AI assistant usually needs a connection. Practise offline: list one task where AI could help and one result you would need to verify.

Complete all three quiz questions to unlock the next lesson.
takeaways: Training uses examples to adjust a model
Inference uses an already trained model

lessons.title: Write a useful prompt
lessons.subtitle: Give the assistant a clear task and constraints
lessons.body:
A prompt is the input you give an AI tool. Start with a specific task, useful context, and the format you want. Add constraints such as length or reading level. Example: Create a five-day study plan for a beginner learning fractions. I have fifteen minutes a day. Return a table with a topic and a practice activity for each day.

Read the first response and ask for a focused revision when needed. Extra instructions can improve relevance but cannot guarantee truth. Practise offline: write a prompt for a study plan, underline the task, circle the context, and mark the requested format.

lessons.title: Check AI answers
lessons.subtitle: Use evidence before trusting a confident response
lessons.body:
AI can give a confident answer that is wrong or invent a reference. Treat factual output as a draft. Identify claims that matter, compare them with an appropriate original source, and check whether cited documents actually exist and support the claim. If evidence is missing, label the claim as unverified.

For a calculation, work through the steps yourself. For changing facts, check the date of the source. Repeating the same question to the same assistant does not provide independent evidence. Practise offline: take the claim Our library opens at 7 a.m. and write how you would verify it when connected, such as checking an official notice.

Complete all three quiz questions to unlock the next lesson.

lessons.title: Protect privacy and fairness
lessons.subtitle: Choose what to share and inspect assumptions
lessons.body:
Before using an online AI tool, consider what information you are sending. Use fictional examples or remove personal details when practising. Do not include passwords or other people’s private information. Read the service’s privacy information and follow the rules of your school or workplace. Removing a name alone may not make a detailed story anonymous.

Generated answers may reflect unfair assumptions about people or omit perspectives. Check who is represented, whose experience is missing, and whether the output is appropriate for your audience. Keep human oversight over decisions. Practise offline: rewrite a sample prompt using fictional names and inspect a draft for assumptions.

Complete all three quiz questions to unlock the next lesson.

lessons.title: Complete your AI practice project
lessons.subtitle: Create, check, and improve a useful study resource
lessons.body:
Choose a small learning task, such as planning revision for a topic you already know. Write a prompt with a clear task, context, format, and limits. You can draft the expected response yourself offline, then optionally try the prompt with an online assistant when connected.

Check the response against your notes or an original source. Correct errors, remove unnecessary personal details, and adapt it to your learning needs. Record what changed and how you checked it. Follow any required disclosure rules for AI assistance. Complete all lesson quizzes before submitting the final course task.

Final task: explain one AI limitation (recap); write and review a study-plan prompt (practice); record a verification plan (plan); show your improved study resource and explain a correction (demonstrate).

Complete all three quiz questions to unlock the next lesson.
